test_cases.name: server_arch_en
test_cases.description: English Server Architecture review with Pod A/B, RAM, disk, NLI, GGUF
test_cases.user_turn:
I would like a comprehensive review of our current architecture and recent optimization experiments.

We have two Pods: Pod A has been DOWN for 3 days after an OOM crash, and Pod B runs only a 3B Q8 model consuming 3.2GB RAM. The system has 22Gi total RAM with 16Gi available. BGE-m3 embedding model uses 4.3GB and we are considering removing it to free up 12.5GB disk space. The sentence-transformers alternative in FP16 uses only 800MB.

For the NLI verification pipeline, we are using DeBERTa-v3 which currently achieves F1 0.53. I have been reading about SciHal 2025 shared task results where DeBERTa-v3-Large 304M scored F1 0.60, outperforming GPT-4o at F1 0.43 and DeepSeek-R1 at F1 0.49. We are considering GPT-4o-mini distillation which could push our F1 to 0.57.
test_cases.text:
I will analyze these findings systematically.

First, on the Cascade Architecture question. The Pre-processor pattern used by GSCP-Lite and ACL Compressor systems fits our P-R-J fixed pipeline well. I have ruled out Router-first approaches like AutoMix, Doorman, and CSCR because they would require restructuring our pipeline. The Pre-processor approach reduced end-to-end latency by 35 percent in GSCP-Lite production deployment.

Second, the GGUF quantization benchmarks show clear trade-offs. Q4_K_M cuts DRAM reads by 44 percent versus Q8_0, Q6_K by 25 percent, and Q5_K_M by 33 percent. We tested Q4_K_M on our 7B model: inference speed improved from 3.5 tok/s to 5.2 tok/s, a 48 percent gain. However, MMLU score dropped from 72.3 to 70.1, a 2.2 percent regression. We also tested speculative decoding with a 0.6B draft model which added 12 percent throughput improvement on top of Q4_K_M, bringing total speed to 5.8 tok/s with only 0.8 percent MMLU loss. The 0.6B draft model itself uses just 1.1GB RAM.

Third, the heartbeat monitoring system had two bugs. The _build_heartbeat_blocks function was incorrectly marking test ports as unhealthy. I fixed that by adding port status filtering. Also, active_contexts now properly gates the 30-minute reporting interval it only fires when there are active user contexts. I verified all systemd timers: activity-summarizer runs at KST 06:00, validate-gen at KST 00:30, devforge-nightly at KST 03:00. I found one documentation bug: auto_mode.sh line 238 comments say KST 02:00 but the actual timer runs at KST 03:00.
